preventive.what: seed treatment, only where bakanae occurred
preventive.why: Bakanae is seed borne; clean certified seed is the first defence and treatment is for seed from infected fields.

preventive.what: molluscicide, only where snails are many
preventive.why: Golden apple snails eat seedlings in the first two weeks; PalayCheck puts canals, screens, hand picking and shallow water first.

preventive.what: herbicide pre emergence
preventive.why: PalayCheck asks for weed control within 0 to 45 DAT; an early residual stops the first grass and sedge flush.

preventive.what: herbicide post emergence, only for escaped weeds
preventive.why: Removes weeds that escaped the residual before they compete at tillering.

preventive.what: no insecticide against leaf feeders
preventive.why: PalayCheck: do not spray defoliators within 30 DAT; spiders and other natural enemies build up and the crop recovers the lost leaf area.

preventive.stage: Late booting to early heading, blast prone variety or area only
preventive.daysAfterPlanting: Late booting and at 5 to 10 percent heading
preventive.what: fungicide
preventive.why: Protects the panicle neck from blast in cool, wet, heavily fertilized fields.

safety: Do not apply propanil within 14 days before or after a carbamate (carbaryl) or organophosphate insecticide; the combination injures rice.
Niclosamide and metaldehyde are toxic to fish; keep treated water in the field and out of fishponds and canals.
PalayCheck: do not spray against defoliators within 30 DAT; insecticide is a last resort after cultural and biological control.
Hold water 3 to 5 days after a pre emergence herbicide and do not drain it into the next field.
Observe the preharvest interval printed on each FPA registered label; Philippine guides require it but leave the number to the label, and residues above limits make produce unsellable.
Rotate IRAC and FRAC groups between sprays; do not spray the same group more than twice in a row.
